prompt:
Write 7 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a rear-end collision claim, in time order. Injury: whiplash. The claimant is represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1228; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury is plausible for a crash like this one.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- No earlier injury to the same body area is known.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- A neighbor thinks the car was damaged some weeks before the claimed date.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim reported by the claimant's representing attorney following a rear-end collision at a signalized intersection. The insured's vehicle was stopped when it was struck from behind by the other driver's vehicle. Policy verified and the driver is named on the policy.

Entry 2: Recorded statement taken from the claimant, who described the impact and the sequence of events. The account given matched what was reported at first notice of loss.

Entry 3: Police report obtained, which places the claimant inside the vehicle at the time of impact. Responding officers and two independent witnesses confirm the collision happened as described.

Entry 4: Photographs of the vehicle reviewed. The rear damage is consistent with the force and direction of the impact described by all parties. A repair estimate has been requested from the shop.

Entry 5: Claimant reports neck and upper back pain with symptoms consistent with whiplash. Medical records show the injury is plausible for a crash of this type, and no prior treatment to the same area appears in the records or in the claimant's history.

Entry 6: Treatment reviewed. Care followed a typical course of physical therapy and follow-up visits, and frequency of treatment has reduced as the claimant's condition improved. Next scheduled review is set for the coming month.

Entry 7: A neighbor contacted the office and stated the vehicle looked damaged a few weeks before the reported loss. No prior damage to the vehicle is known from inspection, repair history or the other driver's account, so the statement is being noted and will be followed up with the shop's records.
